data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise unreal past conditionals and mixed conditionals linking past causes with present results or present states with past outcomes.
learningPoints: Use if + Past Perfect, would have + past participle for Third Conditionals.
Use Third Conditionals for unreal past situations and their imagined past results.
Use mixed conditionals to connect past causes with present results.
Use mixed conditionals to connect present states with past results where appropriate.
Avoid using would in the if-clause.
Choose the conditional type according to the time relationship.

sections.explain: Use IF + Past Perfect, WOULD HAVE + past participle.

words.word: If I had known, I would have called you.
If I would have known, I would have called you.
If I had knew, I would have call you.

sections.explain: The if-clause can be negative with HADN'T + past participle.

words.word: If we hadn't missed the train, we would have arrived on time.
If we wouldn't have missed the train, we would have arrived on time.
If we hadn't miss the train, we would have arrived on time.

sections.explain: The structure is commonly used to imagine a different past outcome.

words.word: She would have passed if she had studied harder.
She would pass if she had studied harder yesterday.
She would have passed if she would have studied harder.

sections.summary: Using a mixed conditional: past cause, present result.
sections.explain: Use Past Perfect in the if-clause and WOULD + base verb for a present result caused by the past.

words.word: If I had taken that job, I would live in London now.
If I took that job, I would have lived in London now.
If I had taken that job, I would have lived in London now as a present-state result.

sections.summary: Using a mixed conditional for a present state caused by a past decision.
sections.explain: Past unreal cause can lead to a present hypothetical result.

words.word: If she had gone to university, she might have a different career now.
If she went to university then, she might have had a different career now.
If she had went to university, she might have a different career now.

sections.summary: Using a mixed conditional: present state, past result.
sections.explain: A present unreal state can be connected to a past hypothetical consequence.

words.word: If I were more organised, I wouldn't have missed the deadline.
If I had been more organised now, I wouldn't miss the deadline yesterday.
If I would be more organised, I wouldn't have missed the deadline.

sections.summary: Using 'could have' in a Third Conditional.
sections.explain: COULD HAVE can express an unreal past possibility.

words.word: If we'd left earlier, we could have avoided the traffic.
If we'd left earlier, we could avoid the traffic yesterday.
If we would have left earlier, we could have avoided the traffic.

sections.summary: Using 'might have' for a less certain past result.
sections.explain: MIGHT HAVE can express an uncertain imagined result.

words.word: If he had applied, he might have got the job.
If he would have applied, he might have got the job.
If he had applied, he might got the job.

sections.explain: Normally, WOULD does not appear in the conditional if-clause.

words.word: If they had listened to the warning, they wouldn't have had the problem.
If they would have listened to the warning, they wouldn't have had the problem.
If they had listened to the warning, they wouldn't had the problem.

sections.explain: Third and mixed conditionals differ according to whether the imagined result is past or present.

words.word: If I hadn't moved abroad, I would still be working at the same company.
If I didn't move abroad, I would have still worked at the same company now.
If I hadn't moved abroad, I would have still be working at the same company.
